q.s: The Sothi-Siswal culture of the Early Harappan phase belongs to which area?
q.x: Sothi-Siswal is the Early Harappan culture of the Rajasthan–Haryana (Ghaggar) area; Hakra belongs to Cholistan.

q.s: Amri and Kot Diji, two important Early Harappan sites, are located in:
q.x: Both Amri and Kot Diji lie in Sindh; Kot Diji was a fortified settlement destroyed by fire.

q.s: Which was the first Harappan site to be excavated after Independence?
q.x: Ropar on the Sutlej (Punjab) was the first Harappan site dug after 1947.

q.s: Dholavira, discovered by J. P. Joshi in 1967-68, was excavated from 1990 by:
q.x: R. S. Bisht excavated Dholavira (1990) and also Banawali.

q.s: Which is the commonest sign in the Harappan script?
q.x: The script is mostly pictographic and the fish sign occurs most often.

q.s: Most of the about 5,000 inscribed objects of the Harappan civilisation are:
q.x: About 3,500 of the roughly 5,000 inscribed objects are seals.

q.s: The Harappan 'signboard' with ten large signs was found at:
q.x: The ten-sign signboard was found near the North Gate of Dholavira.

q.s: Which animal is the commonest motif on Harappan seals?
q.x: The mythical one-horned 'unicorn' is the commonest seal motif.

q.s: Which of the following theory – proponent pairs about the decline of the Harappan civilisation is NOT correctly matched?
o: Shift of the Indus course – H. T. Lambrick
q.x: The Aryan invasion theory is Mortimer Wheeler's; Aurel Stein is linked with climatic change.

q.s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II was composed by:
q.x: Ravikirti wrote the Aihole prashasti; Harisena wrote the Allahabad Pillar prashasti of Samudragupta.

q.s: The Nasik Prashasti on Gautamiputra Satakarni was issued by:
q.x: His mother Gautami Balashri issued the Nasik inscription; Naganika issued the Nanaghat inscription.

q.s: Rakhigarhi, the largest known Harappan site, is located in:
q.x: Rakhigarhi lies in Hisar district of Haryana on the seasonal Drishadvati.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the early Vedic polity?
o: Tribal assemblies like Sabha and Samiti
q.x: The early Vedic polity was kinship-based without a fixed territory; it had no formal bureaucracy.

q.s: Painted Grey Ware (PGW) was first found in 1940–44 at:
q.x: PGW was first found at Ahichchhatra; Hastinapur was dug later by B. B. Lal.

q.s: Painted Grey Ware sites lie mainly in:
o: Upper Ganga basin and Indo-Gangetic divide
q.x: Most of about 700 PGW sites are in the upper Ganga basin and the Indo-Gangetic divide.

q.s: Among the later Vedic ratnins, the Bhagadugha was the:
q.x: Bhagadugha collected revenue (the king's share); the treasurer was the Sangrahitri and the Suta the charioteer.

q.s: Which ratnin acted as the treasurer in the later Vedic period?
q.x: Sangrahitri was the treasurer; Palagala was the messenger.

q.s: Which ancient city was ringed by five hills?
q.x: Rajagriha, the early capital of Magadha, was surrounded by five hills.

q.s: Ujjayini, capital of Avanti, stood on the river:
q.x: Ujjayini (Ptolemy's 'Ozene') was on the Sipra; Kaushambi was on the Yamuna.

q.s: In ancient India, 'Karshapana' referred to:
o: Standard punch-marked silver or copper coin
q.x: Karshapana was the standard punch-marked coin; nishka was a gold ornament and satamana a unit of 100 mana.

q.s: The earliest extant coins of India are:
q.x: Punch-marked coins, bearing symbols but no writing, are the earliest extant Indian coins.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT true of punch-marked coins?
o: They were mostly made of silver
They carried the names of kings
They bore symbols like the sun, trees and hills
They are referred to in Pali texts
q.x: Punch-marked coins bore only symbols, no writing.

q.s: Kotilingala, Dhulikatta and Kondapur were important centres of the:
q.x: These Telangana sites were Satavahana trade and urban centres.

q.s: The ancient Uttarapatha route linked Taxila with:
q.x: The Uttarapatha ran from Taxila through the Ganga valley to Tamralipti; the Dakshinapatha led to the Deccan.

q.s: Who among the following Buddhist scholars is called the 'Father of Indian logic'?
q.x: Dignaga wrote Pramana Samuccaya; Dharmakirti, the 'Kant of India', developed his logic.

q.s: The Abhidharmakosa was written by:
q.x: Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa.

q.s: Which source describes the Jain end of Chandragupta Maurya?
q.x: Hemachandra's Parishishtaparvan describes Chandragupta's Jain end; the Divyavadana carries legends of Ashoka.

q.s: The Mauryan state is often described by historians as a:
q.x: The highly centralised Mauryan state, with the king heading executive, legislature and judiciary, is called a paternal despotism.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the effects of land grants in the Gupta period is correct?
o: Land grants were made only to Brahmanas.
Granted villages continued to pay all taxes to the king.
Royal officials were barred from entering the granted villages.
Land grants were confined to the Gangetic heartland.
q.x: Grants carried immunities barring royal officials; they also went to Buddhist monks and to tribal frontiers, turning tribes into sub-castes.

q.s: The Panchasiddhantika, which summarises five astronomical siddhantas, was written by:
q.x: Varahamihira wrote the Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita and Brihat Jataka.

q.s: Varahamihira's Brihat Jataka is a work on:
q.x: The Brihat Jataka deals with astrology (horoscopy), not medicine.

q.s: Which Chinese traveller came by sea via Srivijaya and studied at Nalanda in the late 7th century?
q.x: I-Tsing came by the sea route via Srivijaya; Fa-Hien visited Gupta India.

q.s: Hiuen-Tsang visited India during the reign of:
q.x: Hiuen-Tsang came in Harsha's reign; Fa-Hien came under Chandragupta II.

q.s: Which of the following Chola revenue terms is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kadamai was land revenue in kind; Nettal was compulsory labour.

q.s: The Turkan-i-Chahalgani ('the Forty') was a:
q.x: The Chahalgani was the corps of forty Turkish nobles formed under Iltutmish.

q.s: Which tomb earned Iltutmish the title 'Father of tomb building'?
q.x: Sultan Ghari, built for his son, is the first Islamic tomb in India; the Qutb Minar is dedicated to Bakhtiyar Kaki.

q.s: Who founded the Tughluq dynasty in 1320 after killing Khusrau Khan?
q.x: Ghazi Malik took the title Ghiyasuddin Tughluq in 1320.

q.s: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, the last Khalji ruler, was murdered by:
q.x: Khusrau Khan killed Mubarak Shah; Malik Kafur had himself been killed earlier.

q.s: Razia, the first woman ruler of Delhi, was the daughter of:
q.x: Iltutmish nominated his daughter Razia as successor.

q.s: Who was the first Afghan ruler of Delhi?
q.x: Bahlol Lodi founded the Lodi dynasty in 1451.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the Diwan-i-Insha dealt with:
q.x: The Diwan-i-Insha under the Dabir-i-Mumalik handled royal correspondence; religious affairs were under the Diwan-i-Risalat.

q.s: Which Sultanate department, under the Chief Sadr, dealt with religious affairs and grants to mosques and madrasas?
q.x: Diwan-i-Risalat handled religious matters; Diwan-i-Arz was the military department.

q.s: Sardeshmukhi, levied by the Marathas, was:
q.x: Sardeshmukhi was an additional one-tenth; chauth was one-fourth.

q.s: The 'amaram' land tenure was a feature of the:
q.x: Amaram lands were held by Vijayanagara nayakas; mokasa was a Maratha term and jagir a Mughal one.

q.s: Dagh (branding of horses) and huliya (descriptive roll of soldiers) were introduced by:
q.x: Alauddin Khalji introduced both; Sher Shah later revived the dagh.

q.s: Which historian held that the state of the Delhi Sultans was not truly Islamic because they ruled through zawabit (state laws)?
q.x: Barani argued that the Sultans followed Persian-style jahandari and governed by zawabit rather than the Sharia.

q.s: The jizya was reimposed in 1679 by:
q.x: Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya in 1679; Akbar had abolished it in 1564.

q.s: Which ruler of Kashmir abolished the jizya and banned cow slaughter?
q.x: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir was noted for tolerance; Sikandar Butshikan was known for the opposite.

q.s: Dara Shikoh commanded the Mughal siege of Kandahar in the year:
q.x: Aurangzeb led the 1649 and 1652 sieges; Dara Shikoh led the failed 1653 siege.

q.s: Who was the first foreign ruler to invade north-west India?
q.x: Darius I of Persia invaded north-west India around 518 BCE.

q.s: The Huna ruler Mihirakula was defeated by:
q.x: Yashodharman of Malwa defeated Mihirakula.

q.s: Under the Mughals, how many copper dams made one rupee?
q.x: Forty dams made one rupiya, the silver coin of 178 grains fixed by Sher Shah.

q.s: The gold coin of the Mughals was the:
q.x: The mohur was gold, the rupiya silver and the dam copper.

q.s: Under Akbar's revenue system, land cultivated every year was called:
q.x: Polaj was cultivated annually; chachar was fallow 3-4 years and banjar 5 years or more.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a category of land in Akbar's revenue classification?
q.x: Amaram was a Vijayanagara tenure; the Mughal categories were polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.

q.s: The Molla Ramayanam was written by:
q.x: The woman poet Atukuri Molla wrote the Molla Ramayanam in simple Telugu.

q.s: Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi was promulgated in:
q.x: Din-i-Ilahi came in 1582; the Ibadat Khana was built in 1575.

q.s: In Maratha administration, 'saranjam' meant:
q.x: Saranjam grants were abolished by Shivaji and restored under Shahu; bagayat was irrigated land and kathi the measuring rod.

q.s: Who was the first French governor and builder of Pondicherry?
q.x: Francois Martin founded and built Pondicherry; Godeheu replaced Dupleix in 1754.

q.s: The French under Count de Lally were defeated at Wandiwash (1760) by:
q.x: Sir Eyre Coote defeated Lally at Wandiwash, ending French power in India.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857, the rising at Bareilly was led by:
q.x: Khan Bahadur Khan led Bareilly; Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah led Faizabad.

q.s: Maniram Dutt led the Revolt of 1857 in:
q.x: Maniram Dutt (Maniram Dewan) led the rising in Assam.

q.s: Which of the following leader – centre pairs of the Revolt of 1857 is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Shah Mal led the rising at Baraut (Baghpat); Fazil Muhammad Khan led Bhopal.

q.s: Mangal Pandey fired at his officers at Barrackpore on:
q.x: He fired on 29 March and was hanged at Barrackpore on 8 April; 10 May is the Meerut outbreak.

q.s: Mangal Pandey belonged to which regiment?
q.x: The 34th BNI was disbanded after his act; 85 sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were jailed at Meerut.

q.s: The Treaty of Surat (1775) was signed by the Bombay government with:
q.x: The Treaty of Surat with Raghunathrao led to the First Anglo-Maratha War.

q.s: The Treaty of Devgaon (1803) was signed by the English with:
q.x: Devgaon was with the Bhonsle; Surji-Arjangaon with Sindhia; Rajpurghat with Holkar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mahalwari system is correct?
o: Revenue was collected by the village headman and the village was collectively liable.
The unit of assessment was the individual ryot.
The land belonged to the government.
It was introduced in Bengal by Cornwallis.
q.x: Under Mahalwari the mahal (village or group of villages) was the unit, the land belonged to the village community, and the lambardar collected revenue.

q.s: The Taluqdari system of land revenue is associated with:
q.x: Taluqdars were the big landholders of Awadh.

q.s: The Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act (1879) was passed after the:
q.x: The 1875 Deccan riots against moneylenders led to the 1879 Act protecting peasants.

q.s: The Punjab Land Alienation Act, which checked the transfer of land to non-agriculturists, was passed in:
q.x: The Punjab Land Alienation Act was passed in 1900.

q.s: Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 from:
q.x: He won Finsbury Central in 1892 after losing at Holborn in 1886.

q.s: At which session of the Congress did Dadabhai Naoroji declare Swaraj as the goal in 1906?
q.x: He presided over the Calcutta session of 1906 and declared Swaraj the goal.

q.s: Udant Martand (1826), the first Hindi newspaper, was started by:
q.x: Jugal Kishore Shukla started Udant Martand at Calcutta.

q.s: Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822) was published in:
q.x: Mirat-ul-Akhbar was in Persian; his Sambad Kaumudi was in Bengali.

q.s: The Police Act of 1861 organised the Indian police on the model of the:
q.x: The 1861 Act followed the Royal Irish Constabulary model.

q.s: Who took police duties away from the zamindars and set up thanas under an Indian daroga?
q.x: Cornwallis created the thana system under a daroga.

q.s: Which of the following statements about local bodies in British India after Ripon's Resolution of 1882 is correct?
o: They remained weak for lack of funds and official control.
Elected members formed a clear majority in district boards.
They were elected on a wide franchise.
They could not be suspended or superseded.
q.x: Despite Ripon's Resolution, local bodies had a narrow franchise, few elected members, little money and could be superseded.

q.s: Ambedkar's Mahad Satyagraha (1927) asserted the right of Dalits to:
o: Draw water from the Chavdar tank
Walk on temple roads at Vaikom
q.x: Mahad was about water from the Chavdar tank; the Kalaram temple entry movement was at Nasik in 1930.

q.s: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha (1930) led by Ambedkar took place at:
q.x: The Kalaram temple is in Nasik.

q.s: R. Venkataratnam Naidu's Brahma Mandir in Andhra was located at:
q.x: Venkataratnam Naidu built the Brahma Mandir at Kakinada.

q.s: Who renamed the Veda Samaj of Madras as the Dakshina Bharata Brahmo Samaj?
q.x: Sridharalu Naidu renamed it and translated Brahmo books into Tamil and Telugu.

q.s: The 'Lone Star' Mission of the American Baptists in Andhra was located at:
q.x: The American Baptist 'Lone Star' Mission worked at Ongole; the Lutherans worked in Guntur.

q.s: Who remarked in 1931 that 'Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust but not the level'?
q.x: Ambedkar made this remark; he also rejected Gandhi's term 'Harijan'.

q.s: The original name of Swami Dayananda Saraswati was:
q.x: Dayananda was born Mool Shankar.

q.s: Swami Dayananda Saraswati was born at:
q.x: He was born at Tankara in Morvi state, studied under Virajananda of Mathura and died at Ajmer in 1883.

q.s: The British Committee of the Indian National Congress, set up in London in 1889, was chaired by:
q.x: Wedderburn chaired the British Committee, whose journal was 'India'.

q.s: The Komagata Maru (1914) was chartered by:
q.x: Baba Gurdit Singh, a Singapore-based contractor, chartered it to carry Indians to Canada.

q.s: The Komagata Maru sailed from Hong Kong to:
q.x: It went to Vancouver, where most of its 376 passengers were refused entry under the 'continuous journey' rule.

q.s: Who was the founder-president of the Ghadar Party?
q.x: Sohan Singh Bhakna was the founder-president; Darsi Chenchaiah was its only Telugu member.

q.s: The autobiography of Darsi Chenchaiah is:
q.x: Darsi Chenchaiah wrote Nenu Naa Desam; Naa Jeevitha Yatra is Prakasam's autobiography.

q.s: Who described the Cripps offer as 'a post-dated cheque'?
q.x: Gandhi called it a post-dated cheque; Nehru called the August Offer's Dominion status 'dead as a doornail'.

q.s: The Muslim League observed 'Day of Deliverance' on:
q.x: The League celebrated the resignation of Congress ministries as the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939.

q.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded the Andhra Bank in 1923 at:
q.x: The Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam.

q.s: 'Feathers and Stones', a diary of imprisonment in Ahmednagar Fort, was written by:
q.x: Pattabhi wrote Feathers and Stones; he also presided over the Jaipur Congress of 1948.

q.s: The first inscriptional use of the term 'Andhrapatha' is found in the:
q.x: The Prakrit Mayidavolu grant of the Pallava Sivaskandavarman (c. AD 300) first uses 'Andhrapatha'.

q.s: The Mayidavolu copper-plate grant was issued by:
q.x: It is a Pallava record, like the Manchikallu inscription.

q.s: The Satavahana capital Dhanyakataka is identified with:
q.x: Dhanyakataka is Dharanikota near Amaravati; Pratishthana is Paithan on the Godavari.

q.s: Who shifted the Satavahana capital east to Dhanyakataka?
q.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi moved the capital east to Dhanyakataka.

q.s: In Satavahana administration, the Heranika was the:
q.x: Heranika was the treasurer; Rajjugahaka the land surveyor and Pattikapala the drafter of grant inscriptions.

q.s: The Chaitika sects of Andhra Buddhism were founded by:
q.x: Mahadeva Bhikshu founded the Chaitika sects.

q.s: The Chaitika sects of Andhra were branches of the:
q.x: They grew out of the Mahasanghika school.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the support of Buddhism in the Satavahana age is correct?
o: Buddhism was patronised only by the kings.
Guilds held money on deposit and paid the interest to the monks.
Foreign merchants gave no support to Buddhist caves.
q.x: Guilds at Nasik, Junnar and Kanheri paid interest to monks, Yavana merchants funded caves, and Prakrit made Buddhism a mass movement.

q.s: A Roman-style amphitheatre of the Ikshvaku period has been found at:
q.x: The amphitheatre is at Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda), the Ikshvaku capital.

q.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the guilds of the Vaisyas (Komatis) were called:
q.x: Vaisya guilds were Nakarams; the Panchanamvaru were the five artisan groups.

q.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the Niyogi Brahmins mainly served in:
q.x: Brahmins split into Vaidikas (priestly) and Niyogis (administration and army).

q.s: The Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot was built by the Eastern Chalukya ruler:
q.x: Danarnava built the Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot.

q.s: Who is called the 'Adikavi' of Telugu?
q.x: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu is the first book in Telugu.

q.s: In the bilingual grants of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi, the prasasti (praise) portion was written in:
q.x: The prasasti stayed in Sanskrit while the grant details were in Telugu.

q.s: Which of the following Kakatiya inscriptions is NOT correctly matched with its subject?
o: Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam – Jain temple grant
Bayyaram tank inscription – Genealogy of early Kakatiyas
q.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam (1244) gave protection to foreign sea traders.

q.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam (1244) for the safety of sea merchants was issued by:
q.x: Ganapatideva issued it, promising compensation for shipwreck and theft.

q.s: Marco Polo visited Motupalli during the reign of:
q.x: Marco Polo came during Rudramadevi's reign and praised her rule.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Reddi kingdom of Rajahmundry is correct?
o: Its first ruler Anavota was the son of Prolaya Vema Reddi.
Kataya Vema Reddi was killed by Krishnadevaraya.
Its capital was later shifted to Addanki.
Allada Reddi ran the state as regent for Veerabhadra Reddi.
q.x: Allada Reddi was regent; Anavota was Kumaragiri's son and Kataya Vema died at Kakaraparthi in 1414.

q.s: Who opened the gate of Golconda fort to the Mughals in 1687?
q.x: Abdullah Khan Pani betrayed the fort; Abdur Razzaq Lari fought on loyally.

q.s: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler, was buried at:
q.x: He died a prisoner at Daulatabad and was buried at Khuldabad.

q.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler was called 'Malkibharama' by Telugu poets?
q.x: Ibrahim, who had lived in exile at Vijayanagara, learnt Telugu and patronised Telugu poets.

q.s: Which of the following Deccan Sultanates did NOT take part in the battle of Talikota (1565)?
q.x: All except Berar fought at Talikota; Ahmadnagar annexed Berar only in 1574.

q.s: Who described the Vijayanagara empire as a 'segmentary state'?
q.x: Burton Stein used the segmentary state model in 'Peasant State and Society in Medieval South India'.

q.s: The 'Rayavachakam' was written by:
q.x: Sthanapati wrote the Rayavachakam.

q.s: The Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara was founded by:
q.x: Vira Narasimha founded the Tuluva line in 1505; Saluva Narasimha founded the Saluva line in 1485.

q.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara was founded by:
q.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty after Talikota.

q.s: The line 'Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa' occurs in:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya wrote it in the preface of his Telugu Amuktamalyada.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Sanskrit work of Krishnadevaraya?
q.x: Amuktamalyada is in Telugu; the others are his Sanskrit works.

q.s: Niti Shastra Muktavali of the Kakatiya period was written by:
q.x: Baddena wrote the Niti Shastra Muktavali; Sivadevayya wrote the Purushartha Saramu.

q.s: Ketana, called 'Abhinava Dandi', wrote the:
q.x: Vignanesvaram is a Telugu rendering of the Mitakshara.

q.s: The Porumamilla inscription (1369) records the building of the Anantasagaram tank by:
o: Prince Bhaskara, son of Bukka I
q.x: Prince Bhaskara (Bhavadura), son of Bukka I, built the tank.

q.s: Porumamilla, known for a Vijayanagara tank inscription, is in:
q.x: Porumamilla is in Kadapa (YSR) district.

q.s: Tadipatri, known for its Vijayanagara-era temples, is in:
q.x: Tadipatri lies in Anantapur district.

q.s: The temples of Tadipatri were patronised by the:
q.x: The Pemmasani Nayakas patronised the Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara temples.

q.s: William Carey's first printed Telugu Bible was produced at:
q.x: The Baptist press at Serampore printed it.

q.s: Who became the first Andhra Mahamahopadhyaya in 1907?
q.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam received the title in 1907.

q.s: The Andhra Jateeya Vidya Parishad (1907) was set up by:
q.x: Kopalle Hanumantha Rao founded it on 17 November 1907 at Machilipatnam.

q.s: Praja Natya Mandali (1943) was the Andhra wing of the:
q.x: Praja Natya Mandali was the Andhra unit of IPTA.

q.s: Which folk art form did the Praja Natya Mandali widely use to carry political messages?
q.x: It made Burrakatha a vehicle of political propaganda.

q.s: 'Veyipadagalu', which won the Sahitya Akademi award, was written by:
q.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana wrote Veyipadagalu.

q.s: 'Andhrula Sanghika Charitra' was written by:
q.x: Suravaram Pratap Reddy wrote this social history of the Andhras.

q.s: 'Mahaprasthanam' was written by:
q.x: Mahaprasthanam is Sri Sri's collection of revolutionary poems.

q.s: Which of the following work – author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: At the Feet of the Master – Gurajada Appa Rao
q.x: At the Feet of the Master is by Jiddu Krishnamurti.

q.s: Tattvabodhini (1864) was published at Madras by the:
q.x: The Madras Veda Samaj published Tattvabodhini.

q.s: Vartamana Tarangini (1842), the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim, was begun by:
q.x: Syed Rahamatullah started it at Madras in 1842.

q.s: Which Telugu newspaper popularised the word 'Andhra' during the Andhra movement?
q.x: Andhra Patrika popularised 'Andhra'; Desabhimani urged Telugu papers to write on Andhra affairs.

q.s: The Bala Bharati Samithi was founded in 1907 at:
q.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, Gante Laxmanna and Unguturi Sriramulu founded it at Rajahmundry.

q.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was expelled during the Vandemataram movement after an incident at:
q.x: He was expelled and blacklisted after the Rajahmundry College incident of 1907.

q.s: The Burrakathas 'Kashtajeevi' and 'Raithu Vijayam' were written by:
q.x: Sunkara Satyanarayana wrote them; Shaik Nazar was the great performer of Burrakatha.

q.s: Who is known as 'Burrakatha Pitamaha'?
q.x: Shaik Nazar popularised Burrakatha with the Praja Natya Mandali.

q.s: The Kharosthi script, written from right to left, was derived from:
q.x: Kharosthi came from the Aramaic script spread by the Achaemenid Persians.

q.s: The satrapy system of north-west India was of which origin?
q.x: The Achaemenid Persians introduced the satrapy system.

q.s: The Vesara style of temple architecture is a blend of:
q.x: Vesara uses a Dravida plan with Nagara details and is found mainly in the Deccan.

q.s: The word 'caste' is derived from the word 'casta' of which language?
q.x: The Portuguese word 'casta' gave us 'caste'.

q.s: Enumeration of caste in the Indian Census began in:
q.x: Caste was enumerated from the 1871 Census; 1931 recorded 4,147 castes.

q.s: Which of the following statements about caste and occupation in India is correct?
o: Industrialisation has strengthened hereditary caste occupations.
The varna system hardened in the Rig Vedic period.
Hereditary occupations have no link with caste status.
Occupational mobility has weakened hereditary occupations.
q.x: Industrialisation and mobility have weakened hereditary occupations; varna hardened only in the Later Vedic period.
